analysis:
The changed files are CI test scripts only: scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py (adds the mimo_audio component to routing tests) and scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (new assertions on the workflow). Neither runs in the provider or coordinator process, so the provider assets (A-001..A-018) and boundaries (TB-002/003/007/009/011/012/013) are not touched directly.

The new tests assert several security-positive CI properties:
- Only pushes to master or dev save caches (SAVE_CACHES), so pull requests cannot poison shared caches.
- Checkouts use persist-credentials: false, so tokens are not saved into the cached .git.
- Cache actions are pinned to commit SHAs.
- The restored .git is validated with git fsck and discarded if damaged.
- The workflow tests still assert no secrets., environment:, id-token: or repository: usage.

The diff does not weaken these assertions. Test-only changes cannot alter runtime controls.

Residual questions, outside the supplied evidence and not provable here:
- The actual ci.yml, action.yml, and ci-component-paths.py changes are not in this batch. Whether they implement what the tests assert, including mimo_audio gating and the .git cache restore-keys scope, is for the other batches to examine.
- Restoring a cached .git from master/dev pushes into PR jobs is a CI supply-chain surface; the tests restrict saves to push events on trusted branches, which is reasonable.
- The sparse-checkout patterns skip only evidence tarballs and landing media.

No finding is reported for this batch. needs_deeper_review is set because the workflow implementation files are not supplied here.
